marta: Heads-up: after the canary we saw a small tail latency bump on host parsing pipeline. 95th went from 180ms -> 260ms. Anyone seen this in traces?
ryan: saw it on the dot — same timeframe. traces show a lot more small syscalls in ingress path.
sophie: profiling said parse_tokens() CPU went up ~35%, but GPU kernel selection still fine.
alex: interesting — did kernel selection logic change? we shipped the kernel-selector heuristics earlier today.
marta: yes, kernel selector 2.1 rolled out at 09:12. It switches for sequences < 128 to fast-atten path.
ryan: but the host-side cost is tokenization + grpc framing. The selector reduces GPU time but increases host CPU because we prefix-reserialize for small seqs.
sophie: kv-cache stats: read latency for cold-key path increased — higher contention on kvcache shard 3.
alex: can you paste the hotpath flame?
sophie: ```flamegraph top: parse_tokens -> normalize_utf8 -> writev -> grpc_sendmsg -> kvcache_lookup -> syscall:writev```
sophie: writev spikes are correlated with HTTP/2 head-of-line fragmentation.
marta: hypotheses: (1) kernel change increases prefix/metadata size -> more writev chunks (2) batcher heuristics now multiplex smaller requests causing more small writes
ryan: I can repro locally with loadgen. Running batch size 4, model small seqs -> see 2x writev calls per request.
alex: solution idea: coalesce writev at proxy, or delay flush for 1ms to let more tokens accumulate.
sophie: also consider lightweight aggregator in proxy that concatenates frames for same connection.
marta: before we change proxy, can we tweak host batching heuristic? Increase minibatch window from 2ms -> 5ms for small seqs.
ryan: tried that in a dev canary: tail reduced from 260ms -> 195ms, but p50 unchanged. CPU increased a bit.
alex: cost tradeoff: 5ms add to latency for ultra-low latency reqs, but improves throughput. Need experiment matrix.
marta: any impact on KV eviction? sophie?
sophie: small window increases concurrent K/V lookups slightly; eviction rate up ~4%, but hit-rate stable.
ryan: also noticed grpc overhead: hpack encoding per small header repeated. Could use header caching for frequent keys.
alex: we have header-cache RFC drafted. if we implement, grpc writev drops ~20%.
marta: action items: (1) ryan run controlled canary with minibatch window 5ms (2) alex prototype proxy coalescer (3) sophie gather kvcache shard metrics for next 6 hours (4) marta run cost/regression analysis
ryan: I'll post perf numbers in this thread later.
alex: +1. tagging @eng-ml in case kernel-selector revert is needed.
infra-bot: Canary deployment 2.1 -> 2.1.1 started by marta at 09:45.
marta: thanks — let's sync 10:30 to decide the path. :calendar:
